sound_direction_sha256_note: Computed mechanically by the director as creative_production.fingerprint(storyboard.creative_direction.sound). The vo-director had no shell and left it null.

take_plan.alignment: Measured captions and the acoustic word stream decide every timing. The authored clock in narration_picture is provisional and approves no timing.
take_plan.breath_rule: Breaths are breaths at full stops. Every sentence is short and ends in a full stop and a normal breath, so no silence is planned inside a sentence and no duration appears in this file or in any prompt text.
take_plan.length_rule: Nothing here stretches speech. If the measured read runs long, the fix is a shorter line by story correction.

overall: One connected read as a plainspoken Texan explaining what a university published. Not a news anchor, no hush, no bright lift. Natural breaths at full stops, no long holds. Say UT and AI as letters, San Antonio with the Texas stress, and the figure as one number.
performance_arc: Plain and close over the flooded yard, quicker through the station and its marks, a lift on the chip turn, steady through the radio ranges, then level and measured on the report of the chip AI and its figure, quietest on the field limit, and the close at the same pace.

director_edit_note: Proposal r9 (not applied): fifteen short sentences replace nine long ones, with board-only revisions after the R8 review (event-aware shot boundaries, chip-glow push of at least one second, s7 trimmed to fit the 9.5 s ceiling at the slow envelope) so each measured caption cue is one sentence of at most 64 characters. The close references no other line by number. No word of the failed takes is named in a synth-facing field. The word that take 6 distorted no longer appears in the script. Editor-only fields were regenerated. Scene-level lines added because vo_synth refuses a direction whose line count differs from the scene count; per-sentence lines retained under sentence_lines. Lines carry no text field because the script has one sentence per file line.
